lesson_title: The Price of an Hour: Gross Pay, Scales and Overtime
hook_text: Not all hours cost the same. Your Sunday is worth DOUBLE.
clip_script: Why should one hour of work cost more than another? Stand in the worker's shoes on a Sunday morning. Everyone else is resting; you're unpacking a stock delivery. Your normal hour costs the shop forty rand — but this is not a normal hour. This is your weekend, your rest. So the price list has three rows: ordinary hours, the plain price — R40. Evening overtime, the plain price plus half again — R60 — like a small apology added to every hour. Sundays and public holidays? DOUBLE — R80 — because those hours cost you the most to give. The only trap: multiplying extra hours by the plain price out of habit. Beat it with one habit of your own — before touching the hours, ask: which row of the price list am I on?
visual_style: A glowing three-row price list (R40 / R60 / R80) with hours as coins dropping into each row; a calendar flipping from weekday to Sunday as the price doubles.
pacing: Steady build through the three rows, snap emphasis on DOUBLE, quick close on the trap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build a gross pay from scratch — rows first, hours second.
